why: A skipped check is not a passed check.  Actions run #3 (2026-08-20) was the
first time this suite ran on a machine that is not Panya's bridge, and four
tests went red because they reached for evidence that a clone cannot have.
The fix is a skip with a declared reason - but an unpinned skip is how a real
test drifts into the skip pile without anybody noticing, so every skip this
suite is allowed to produce is written down here, by module, with a count.
tools/pf_pytest_precondition_census.py compares this file against what pytest
actually reported and goes red when they disagree IN EITHER DIRECTION.
HOW AN ENTRY IS EVALUATED (computed on the spot, never quoted):
expected = 0        if the module was excluded from this pytest selection
expected = 0        if the precondition's artifact IS present on this machine
expected = 'count'  otherwise
So the same pin file is correct on the bridge (all artifacts present, nothing
excluded: 1 skip total) and on a fresh clone in CI (artifacts absent, the
client/corpus modules excluded: 4 skips).  Neither number is hand-typed for a
machine; both fall out of the same rule.
ONE ARTIFACT IS NOT A FILE (round 118, 2026-08-21).  original_schema_history and
audit_head_history are commits, not paths: the evidence is INSIDE git, and what a
machine can lack is the DEPTH of the clone that holds it.  A cloud round clones
shallow, so tests that read a historical blob died with a raw CalledProcessError
and read as a red main on a tree nobody had touched.  Both machines that decide
anything hold the whole history - the gate checks out with fetch-depth: 0 - so
these two keys are present there and expect ZERO skips, exactly like a bridge
artifact that is present.  Same rule, different kind of artifact.
AND ONE WARNING THAT COST A REWRITE.  A path either exists or it does not, but
git can fail to answer for reasons that have nothing to do with the clone: no
git on the machine, not a work tree, a corrupt object store, a wrong SHA.  The
first draft called every one of those 'absent', which meant the guarded tests
skipped and THIS census - asking the same object the same broken question -
agreed and printed PASS.  Deleting .git made the whole suite green.  So those
two keys are classified rather than tested: only a repository that says it is
SHALLOW, or a partial clone that cannot produce the object, may skip; anything
else FAILS the test with the measured reason.  A skip here is a statement about
the clone, never about the machine.
TO CHANGE A NUMBER HERE you must change it in the same commit as the test that
moved it, exactly as COVERAGE_EVIDENCE_DEBT_PIN says about itself.  Round 105
spent a whole round on two pins that were measured before a fix and published
after it; do not add a third.

The gate checks out with fetch-depth: 0 and the bridge holds the whole history, so on both machines that decide anything this expects ZERO skips and the assertions run at full strength.  The guard names the BLOB and not only the commit, because a partial clone has the commit and not the blob.

All three run tools/pf_multiplayer_readiness_audit.py, which re-derives its published suite size from commit 5cc0eda and fails its own historical pin when git cannot hand that commit over.  Separate key from original_schema_history because a clone can hold one commit and not the other: measured 2026-08-21, a clone of the cloud round's own shape held 5cc0eda and not 5c200e2, so one shared key would have skipped these three where they could run.  Do not read a fixed distance out of this note - where a given --depth grafts moves with every commit on main, and the day 5cc0eda falls outside a cloud clone these three skip for a measured reason instead of running, which is the design and not a surprise.  test_two_runs_produce_identical_output stays unguarded on purpose, but not because it is strong: it compares the tool's stdout across two runs and asserts nothing about the exit code, so it is equally green over a tool that fails identically twice.  It is unguarded because it is true everywhere, not because it is evidence.

windows_gate_excluded_modules.note: R170 (Panya ruling 2026-08-25 21:10 +07:00, item 4).  The Windows gate hides WHOLE modules with --ignore, chosen by grepping tests/*.py for a two-word pattern that also matches a COMMENT: writing that word into a test file deletes the module from the gate silently while the gate stays green.  The number was printed twice (the gate's EXCLUDED line, and the census line 'modules excluded from the selection') and graded nowhere - and it is graded in the dangerous direction, because tools/pf_pytest_precondition_census.py uses the exclusion list only to lower expectations to zero, so the more the gate hides the less there is to go red.  It is pinned here and re-derived from the workflow's own formula by tests/test_pytest_precondition_census.py::WindowsGateExclusionPinTests.  Move it only in the same commit that moves the list, and say which module moved and why.  ON THE NUMBER: the R168 letter reported 49 and the ruling quotes that figure; 49 is the RAW pattern-match count.  The gate puts tests/test_foundation_legacy_seam.py back (the -ne clause), so the count of modules actually hidden is 48 - the same off-by-one round 115 already caught and rejected once (43 vs 44), and the number the gate itself prints.  48 is what is pinned; if Panya wants the raw match count pinned instead, both this value and derive() move together.  R172 (COO order 2026-08-25 23:35 +07:00, item 5): the sorted MEMBERSHIP is pinned alongside the number in "modules".  The count alone stayed green when one module drifted in and another drifted out in the same commit; the list closes that.  The price is real and is accepted deliberately: every new test module that mentions GameClient or capture_v141 now has to move this list in the same commit, and the failure message says so.  The number is kept beside it as a human-readable checksum, and a test refuses the two disagreeing. R172 adversary finding 7, recorded rather than quietly rounded: 48 is the number of --ignore ARGUMENTS, not the number of test modules hidden.  tests/pf_preconditions.py is in the list and is not a test_*.py file, so pytest never collects it and hiding it hides nothing - 47 collectible modules are actually hidden.  Both numbers are true of different things; the pin grades the arguments because that is what the gate builds.  R172 adversary finding 1: this list is ALSO now graded against the file the gate itself writes, by tools/pf_pytest_precondition_census.py gate_exclusion_drift(), because the pytest class re-derives it from the workflow's Select-String formula and three measured mutations change what the gate hides without touching that formula.
